Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Priya, Ethan, Samir, Lena, Aaron (TidalWave)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
TidalWave is evaluating reseller partnership with Redwood for GPU-backed inference solutions. Primary asks: resale economics, private/VPC deployment options for enterprise customers, onboarding and support model, and a pilot to validate performance (latency/cost) for a target customer. Security and compliance (SOC2, KMS, SSO) are front-of-mind. Redwood AE/SE outlined Dedicated vs Private options and proposed a 1-week pilot and a partner pricing deck.

Topics: reseller economics, private deployment (VPC/on-prem), pilot scope, compliance, integration points (SSO/KMS), benchmarking, go-to-market motions and enablement

Action items (recorded in-call): Maya to share deck; Daniel to share pilot checklist; Priya to send infra constraints.

--- Transcript body ---
[00:00] Maya: alright everyone thanks for joining, I'm Maya, account exec at Redwood, and with me is Daniel our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing over at TidalWave?
[00:05] Priya: good, thanks, a little crammed on schedule so appreciate you making time.
[00:08] Ethan: yeah hi, Ethan here, CTO, trying to jump in on partner programs that can help our platform customers get faster inference.
[00:13] Daniel: hey Ethan, nice to meet you. quick note — I might jump into a few technical bits, but we'll try to keep it structured.
[00:18] Samir: Samir, infra lead. we manage the clusters and storage; we'll need to validate networking and VPC constraints.
[00:23] Maya: perfect. objective for today is to frame a potential reseller / channel partnership and surface technical blockers for a pilot. we'll cover pricing model, deployment modes — hosted, dedicated, private — and a lightweight benchmark plan.
[00:33] Aaron: and I'm on partnerships, i'll look at co-sell motions.
[00:36] Lena: Lena for ops — curious about support SLAs and handoffs.

[00:40] Maya: quick question to start — what's the primary go-to-market angle? do you want to resell Redwood hosted API to your customers, or bundle Dedicated capacity, or offer private on-prem packages?
[00:52] Priya: mostly reseller-hosted to start, but we have inbound enterprise customers asking for VPC options and some on-prem needs for regulated ones. so a hybrid thing.
[01:02] Ethan: yes, default is resale of hosted for speed to market. for 2-3 large customers we need either a Dedicated pool or a Private VPC deployment behind their firewall.
[01:12] Daniel: ok makes sense. the tradeoffs we usually see — hosted is easiest to spin up and cheaper opex for small customers; Dedicated gives predictable latency and throughput; Private brings more ops work but solves data residency.
[01:24] Priya: cost is a big factor for some of our customers — they compare per-token hosted costs vs committed capacity. we'll need clear economics to sell.

[01:30] [01:30] Daniel: (murmur) and we have batching / kv-cache strategies that lower per-token unit costs if patterns are stable.
[01:34] [01:34] Ethan: could you explain KV cache again — sorry audio cut—
[01:37] Daniel: sure, sorry, kv cache is like keeping large parts of the model state between calls to avoid recomputing; it helps for chat-style sessions and reduces token compute. it relies on sticky routing and session affinity.

[01:50] Priya: okay that sounds useful. what are common enterprise blockers — SSO, audit logs, KMS?
[01:57] Maya: all of the above. we support SAML/SSO for console access and API keys for programmatic. for Private deployments we integrate with customer KMS/HSM and supply audit logs. most compliance asks are covered but we can share the SOC2 pack.
[02:12] Samir: when you say "integrate with KMS" — do you need outbound connectivity or can we provide offline keys? we have customers that require no external key egress.
[02:22] Daniel: good question. for our standard Private package we can support customer-managed KMS with no plaintext keys leaving the customer's environment — HSM integration on-prem. when air-gapped, there's an on-prem bundle — but that does add lead time.

[02:38] Ethan: lead time example?
[02:40] Daniel: typical on-prem full install is 6-8 weeks including validation; a VPC private deployment is usually 2-4 weeks depending on network rules. hosted and Dedicated provisioning takes days.

[02:52] Priya: ok useful. for reseller customers we're mainly selling to SaaS companies; we need a quick pilot to show latency and cost per inference. can Redwood do a 1-week pilot against a TidalWave-managed sample workload?
[03:04] Maya: yes, that's exactly what we propose. Daniel will own the benchmark plan. we'll need a sample prompt set, target latency SLOs, and a list of customer-size profiles (qps, session length).

[03:14] [03:14] Daniel: I'll put together a checklist — minimal infra inputs: sample model (or choose from Redwood catalog), average sequence length, expected peak qps, and whether KV cache should be used. then we'll run hosted and Dedicated variants to compare.
[03:26] Priya: one wrinkle — some customers use quantized models. does Redwood run 4-bit / 8-bit quant?
[03:31] Daniel: yes, our runtime supports multiple quantization profiles, though throughput/latency differs. we'll make recommendations. sometimes there's a quality vs latency trade; we'll flag that in the benchmark.

[03:42] Ethan: what about GPUs — can you support A100 and H100 class? and are there partners you work with for additional capacity?
[03:49] Maya: we certify on common datacenter GPUs, H100/A100; for channel partners we have recommendations and sometimes co-sell with cloud partners. (mumble) some of our partners like OrionCloud and NimbleGPU show up in capacity discussions.

[04:01] Samir: also network egress — for private deployments the customer insists on no internet egress for inference requests. how do you handle model updates and telemetry without egress?
[04:10] Daniel: we can configure local-only control planes with a sync window under customer control; telemetry can be buffered and pulled via secure line. for zero-egress requirements we recommend the on-prem packaged installer.

[04:23] Lena: on support, what's the RTO/RPO for Dedicated customers?
[04:27] Maya: Dedicated includes SLA targets — typical is 99.9 availability SLA and prioritized support for production lanes. details are in the partner playbook deck. for channel partners we also offer a white-glove onboarding package.

[04:39] [04:39] Priya: interested in revenue share — are you flexible? we want a model that allows TidalWave to resell with 20-30% margin for go-to-market.
[04:47] Maya: we have a partner tiering structure. for resellers we can do discounted list pricing plus co-selling credits. exact numbers depend on committed volume, marketing funds, and whether you take on support first-line. I can share a draft term sheet.

[04:59] Ethan: what about co-branded deployment? we want to present as part of our platform —how tight is integration?
[05:05] Daniel: you can white-label the UI for your customers when integrating via our API. for deeper integration we provide SDKs and sample deployment manifests.

[05:14] Priya: okay, let's talk technical blockers specifically — Samir has a list. Samir?
[05:18] Samir: yeah main points: VPC peering constraints (we can't open random ports), cert management, and we want to understand how session affinity can be enforced with our LB (we use envoy). also need to confirm GPU isolation for multi-tenant customers.
[05:32] Daniel: envoy is fine — we support Envoy or nginx for ingress. session affinity we do via sticky routing token in our routing layer. GPU isolation for Dedicated is enforced at runtime — pools are per-tenant but we'll document the limits and isolation surfaces.

[05:44] [05:44] Ethan: any friction with RBAC and SSO? we use Okta SAML.
[05:48] Maya: SAML Okta is standard, we can provision roles and map groups. for API-level RBAC we support token scoping and route-level permissions.

[05:56] Priya: on PCI/PHI customers, data residency and audit logs are must-haves. can we get sample audit log format?
[06:02] Daniel: yes we'll share sample logs. logs include token-level metadata, request latencies, and model versions. we can redact content depending on policy.

[06:10] Lena: what about billing — can we invoice through TidalWave to end-customers?
[06:14] Maya: reseller invoicing is supported. options: you resell at list + margin and invoice customers, or we invoice and pass rebates. we'll map options in the deck.

[06:22] Aaron: go-to-market — if we co-sell, what enablement do you offer?
[06:26] Maya: partner portal, sales playbooks, demo scripts, joint webinars, and 1:1 training for your sales engineers. we also provide technical enablement for pilots.

[06:36] [06:36] Priya: pipeline pull-through — what commitments do you expect from us to get partner pricing?
[06:40] Maya: typically commit to minimum quarterly volume and co-marketing activities; we'll be flexible early-stage. we'll sketch numbers in the term sheet.

[06:48] Samir: last technical detail — for benchmarking, can we instrument token-level breakdowns (CPU vs GPU time) and see model kernel metrics?
[06:55] Daniel: yes our console provides token-level cost/latency breakdowns and per-model kernel profiling for the runtime. for pilots we can share deeper tracing artifacts.

[07:04] Priya: perfect. next, pilot scope — what do you need from us to stand up a 1-week pilot?
[07:10] Daniel: checklist — 1) sample workload and prompt set, 2) target SLOs (p95 latency), 3) peak and baseline qps, 4) any model variants (quantized or not), 5) network constraints and whether we can run hosted vs Dedicated, 6) integration points for telemetry (splunk/elk).

[07:28] Ethan: we can provide a sample customer payload and expected latency < 120ms p95 for small messages, and higher for long contexts. typical qps 50-200 per instance.

[07:36] Maya: good. Daniel will draft the checklist and the pilot costing.

[07:40] [07:40] Aaron: timeline? we want to present to our product council next week and if all goes well start a pilot before holiday slow-down.
[07:47] Maya: short timeline possible — I'll send deck and a proposed pilot kickoff date. Daniel can probably spin up hosted configs within 48-72 hours and Dedicated comparison will take longer.

[07:57] Priya: security review — we'll have our compliance team ask for SOC2 and pen test evidence.
[08:02] Maya: we'll attach our SOC2 report and a security packet. if you need a third-party pen-test summary we can share redacted results.

[08:10] Samir: and network whitelists for VPC — we'll share a template.

[08:14] Daniel: great — also small note on versioning: we'll pin a model version for the pilot so we can reproduce results. runtime can pin and we can do canary rollouts later.

[08:25] Priya: pricing question — any channel discounts for a pilot?
[08:29] Maya: yes we can offer pilot credits and a discounted pilot rate; long-term discounts depend on volume. I'll outline ranges in the deck.

[08:36] [08:36] Ethan: competitor question — some customers asked about NimbleGPU's cheaper reserve pricing; how do you differentiate?
[08:42] Maya: we differentiate on operational guarantees, tooling for throughput/latency optimization, and the unified dev experience across hosted/dedicated/private. also our cost toolkit helps tune batch/kv cache to lower effective unit cost.

[08:55] Priya: okay sounds promising. final wrap — who owns what next?
[09:00] Maya: recap: Maya send partner deck + draft term sheet (due 12-11). Daniel send pilot checklist and a short benchmark plan (due 12-10). Priya share compliance questions and pilot contacts (due 12-15). Samir share infra diagram & network template (due 12-12). we'll tentatively schedule pilot kickoff week of 12-20.

[09:18] Lena: that's good. we'll reconvene after we review the deck.
[09:22] Maya: thanks everyone. any other questions?
[09:24] Aaron: none here.
[09:25] Ethan: all good.
[09:26] Maya: awesome, we'll follow up in email. thanks all, bye.
